card.title: Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act of 2026

companion.label: S. 4559
companion.title: Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act of 2026

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini. (rated before the current eligibility rules; kept)

summary: The Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act of 2026 amends the Federal Power Act to direct the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and the Department of Energy (DOE) to establish rules and procedures for managing the connection of large energy-using facilities (such as data centers exceeding 50 megawatts) to the interstate electricity transmission system. It requires large load customers to pay the full costs of interconnection studies and network upgrades, meet demand-flexibility and new generation requirements, and face measures designed to deter speculative grid requests and protect electricity reliability and consumer affordability.

affected_groups.effect: Must pay 100 percent of interconnection study and network upgrade costs, adhere to strict queue management rules, demonstrate demand flexibility, ensure new generation sources, and report operational data to the Department of Energy.
affected_groups.group: Large Load Customers and Data Center Owners

affected_groups.effect: Required to issue multiple final rules, revise pro forma interconnection procedures, establish queue management best practices, and review transmission tariffs and cost allocation methodologies.

Tasked with collecting data center metrics, establishing an artificial intelligence testbed, providing technical assistance to transmission providers, and compiling a comprehensive report for Congress.
affected_groups.group: Department of Energy (DOE) and National Laboratories

affected_groups.effect: Must update tariffs, implement load interconnection queues, enforce study deposits and milestone payments, and ensure interconnections do not violate grid reliability standards.
Protected from having the transmission costs and network upgrades necessitated by large load facilities shifted onto their rates.

key_provisions: Requires FERC to issue final rules within one year establishing standard interconnection procedures and a formal load interconnection queue system for large load facilities exceeding 50 megawatts.

Mandates that large load customers pay 100 percent of the costs for interconnection studies and nonrefundable payments for all assigned network upgrades, with no cost-shifting to other transmission or retail customers.

Requires large load customers seeking interconnection to demonstrate technical capability for demand flexibility and curtailability, and to guarantee the arrangement of new generating resources to temporally match their capacity needs.

Grants priority in load interconnection queues to large load facilities that use battery backup systems, meet specific prevailing wage and registered apprenticeship construction standards, or enter into labor peace agreements for new energy supply resources.

Directs transmission providers to offer colocated large load facilities non-firm transmission access and non-firm injection rights, while assessing gross-demand charges for ancillary and black start services.

Authorizes the Secretary of Energy to collect specific energy and water performance data from data center owners and operators while exempting that confidential business information from Freedom of Information Act disclosures.

Directs the Department of Energy to establish a data-center-scale artificial intelligence testbed at a National Laboratory within 180 days to research energy efficiency, grid integration, and load flexibility.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act of 2026 amends the Federal Power Act to direct the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and the Department of Energy (DOE) to establish rules and procedures for managing the connection of large energy-using facilities (such as data centers exceeding 50 megawatts) to the interstate electricity transmission system. It requires large load customers to pay the full costs of interconnection studies and network upgrades, meet demand-flexibility and new generation requirements, and face measures designed to deter speculative grid requests and protect electricity reliability and consumer affordability.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a comprehensive federal regulatory framework specifically governing the rapid load growth driven by data centers and artificial intelligence. By shifting 100% of network upgrade and study costs onto large load customers, imposing strict grid reliability and demand flexibility prerequisites, and authorizing federal data collection and research, the bill aims to prevent rate surges for everyday consumers and protect interstate grid stability. The legislation alters how large technology infrastructure connects to the national power grid.
